data.title: Africa CDC Head Pushes For Reappointment Amid Allegations Of Intimidation, ‘Extravagant’ Spending And Adverse Audit Find
data.content:
At the same time, the Ebola outbreak has required the deployment of new field personnel – and is likely a major factor in the creation of new positions in 2026. Africa CDC alludes to this, telling Health Policy Watch: “In an active outbreak, speed is decisive, and the ALD [appointments of limited duration] modality allows qualified personnel to be deployed quickly”. [...] The new members, who attended an orientation meeting on 10 November, are from  Cameroon, Gabon, Gambia, Kenya, Namibia, Sierra Leone, Uganda and Zimbabwe. (North Africa has not yet nominated its two representatives.)

The governing board is due to discuss Kaseya’s reappointment at its first official meeting on 22 November – apparently based on an April assessment conducted by the AU Commission Chairperson. Outside observers expect the process to be a virtual rubber-stamp. [...] Shortly after Kaseya’s appointment to lead Africa CDC in February 2023, the Presidency of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) hailed it as a “great diplomatic victory and recognition of Congolese competence on a global scale”, adding that the appointment was “the epilogue of a long, secret diplomatic battle waged for six months by President Félix Tshisekedi”.
